        {"source": "spec", "quote": "NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40"}
      ],
      "impact": "The FCC's I2C scan or driver calls to address 0x40 would get no response from the PWM driver, so servo outputs would not be driven.",
      "confidence": 0.4
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["FCC2", "NAVC2"],
      "pins": ["FCC2.11", "FCC2.27", "FCC2.50", "FCC2.75", "FCC2.100", "FCC2.21", "NAVC2.19", "NAVC2.32", "NAVC2.48", "NAVC2.64"],

        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"216\") (name \"unconnected-(FCC2-VDD-Pad11)\") (class \"Default\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"276\") (name \"unconnected-(NAVC2-VDD-Pad19)\") (class \"Default\")"}
      ],
      "impact": "If these pins are really unconnected, the MCUs would have no core supply and would not boot.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    },
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["REG3", "U9", "U6", "U8", "U17", "C77", "C2"],
      "pins": ["REG3.1", "U9.3", "U8.4", "U17.28"],
      "nets": ["+3.3V", "+3V3"],
      "observed": "The LDO output (REG3 pin 1) and the sensor and PWM supplies sit on net '+3.3V', while the MCU-side decoupling and pull-ups sit on a separate net '+3V3'. No connection between them appears in the netlist, so the 3.3 V rail appears split into two nets.",
      "expected": "A single 3.3 V distribution net that connects the LDO output to the MCUs, sensors and pull-ups.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"1\") (name \"+3.3V\") (class \"Default\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"2\") (name \"+3V3\") (class \"Default\")"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "3.3 V LDO (MCUs + sensors) | ST LD39200PU33R"}
      ],
      "impact": "The MCU-side 3V3 rail would have no regulator source, so the MCUs and pull-ups would be unpowered or power-starved.",
      "confidence": 0.25
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The netlist shows the PCA9685 address pin A0 tied high, which conflicts with the spec's 0x40 address, and the MCU VDD pins and the 3.3 V rail appear disconnected from the LDO output. These are plausible deviations, but the reference design may share the same wiring, so confidence is moderate."

anomalies.observed: PCA9685PW address pin A0 (U17 pin 1) is tied to the +3.3V net, so it is held high. All other address pins (A1 to A5) are tied to GND.
anomalies.expected: With A0 high, the PCA9685 7-bit address becomes 0x41 rather than the 0x40 the spec lists for this part. Address pins should be low for 0x40.
anomalies.impact: The FCC's I2C scan or driver calls to address 0x40 would get no response from the PWM driver, so servo outputs would not be driven.

anomalies.observed: None of the FCC2 VDD pins or its VDDA pin is on any rail. The +3V3 net contains only NAVC2 pin 1 (VBAT) and no MCU core supply pins. The NAVC2 VDD pins are also isolated.
anomalies.expected: The spec says 3V3 feeds both MCUs. Every VDD and VDDA pin of an STM32 should be tied to the 3.3 V rail.

evidence.quote: 3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: If these pins are really unconnected, the MCUs would have no core supply and would not boot.

anomalies.expected: A single 3.3 V distribution net that connects the LDO output to the MCUs, sensors and pull-ups.
anomalies.impact: The MCU-side 3V3 rail would have no regulator source, so the MCUs and pull-ups would be unpowered or power-starved.
